name: CLEAR corpus (CommonLit Ease of Readability)
summary: About 5,000 reading passages for grades 3 to 12, with readability scores from teachers' judgments and their genre and publication details.

license.note: CommonLit's announcement says the dataset and metadata are MIT; the GitHub README says CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Each passage also has its own license: many are public domain, some non-commercial or no-derivatives.

cite: Crossley, S., Heintz, A., Choi, J. S., Batchelor, J., Karimi, M., & Malatinszky, A. (2023). A large-scaled corpus for assessing text readability. Behavior Research Methods, 55(2), 491-507. https://doi.org/10.3758/s13428-022-01802-x

fits.how: No slot yet: its passages, chosen by their own licenses, could be an activity's readings, and its scores could check how an agent pitches a text's difficulty.

connect.note: Comes down as its spreadsheet. XLSX, which the harness doesn't read, and each passage has its own license, so nothing is made from it. Asks you to accept its unclear license first.
